metadata.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System

nodes.name: Tree Ensemble Model
nodes.statement: For data $\mathcal{D}=\{(\mathbf{x}_i,y_i)\}$ with $|\mathcal{D}|=n$, $\mathbf{x}_i\in\mathbb{R}^m$, the model uses $K$ additive regression trees: $\hat{y}_i=\phi(\mathbf{x}_i)=\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(\mathbf{x}_i)$, $f_k\in\mathcal{F}$, where $\mathcal{F}=\{f(\mathbf{x})=w_{q(\mathbf{x})}\}$ is the space of regression trees (CART).
nodes.statement_clean: Tree ensemble: prediction is the sum of K regression-tree outputs.

nodes.name: Regularized Learning Objective
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}(\phi)=\sum_i l(\hat{y}_i,y_i)+\sum_k \Omega(f_k)$ where $\Omega(f)=\gamma T+\tfrac{1}{2}\lambda\|w\|^2$, with $T$ the number of leaves and $w$ the leaf weights.
nodes.statement_clean: Loss plus per-tree complexity penalty on leaf count and L2-norm of leaf weights.

nodes.name: Instance Set of Leaf
nodes.statement: $I_j=\{i\mid q(\mathbf{x}_i)=j\}$ is the set of training instances mapped to leaf $j$ by tree structure $q$.

nodes.name: Gradient Statistics $g_i, h_i$
nodes.statement: $g_i=\partial_{\hat{y}^{(t-1)}} l(y_i,\hat{y}^{(t-1)})$ and $h_i=\partial^2_{\hat{y}^{(t-1)}} l(y_i,\hat{y}^{(t-1)})$ are the first and second order gradient statistics of the loss at iteration $t$.

nodes.name: Rank Function for Feature $k$
nodes.statement: For multiset $\mathcal{D}_k=\{(x_{1k},h_1),\dots,(x_{nk},h_n)\}$, $r_k(z)=\frac{1}{\sum_{(x,h)\in\mathcal{D}_k}h}\sum_{(x,h)\in\mathcal{D}_k,\,x<z} h$ is the proportion of $h$-weighted instances with feature value $<z$.

nodes.name: Quantile Summary of Weighted Data
nodes.statement: $Q(\mathcal{D})=(S,\tilde{r}^+,\tilde{r}^-,\tilde{\omega})$ with $S=\{x_1<\cdots<x_k\}\subseteq\mathcal{D}$, $x_1=\min$, $x_k=\max$, satisfying $\tilde{r}^-(x_i)\leq r_\mathcal{D}^-(x_i)$, $\tilde{r}^+(x_i)\geq r_\mathcal{D}^+(x_i)$, $\tilde{\omega}(x_i)\leq \omega_\mathcal{D}(x_i)$, plus monotone-spacing constraints.
nodes.statement_clean: Compact summary that under-/over-approximates the weighted ranks of selected sample points.

nodes.name: Extension of Function Domains
nodes.statement: Extends $\tilde{r}^-,\tilde{r}^+,\tilde{\omega}$ from $S$ to all $y\in\mathcal{X}$: zeros below $x_1$, plateau above $x_k$, and for $y\in(x_i,x_{i+1})$ set $\tilde{r}^-(y)=\tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)$, $\tilde{r}^+(y)=\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})$, $\tilde{\omega}(y)=0$.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-Approximate Quantile Summary
nodes.statement: $Q(\mathcal{D})$ is $\epsilon$-approximate if $\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{r}^-(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)\leq \epsilon\,\omega(\mathcal{D})$ for all $y\in\mathcal{X}$.

nodes.name: Block (CSC Column Storage)
nodes.statement: An in-memory unit storing data in compressed-column (CSC) format with each column pre-sorted by its feature value; computed once and reused across iterations.

nodes.name: Second-order Approximation of Boosting Objective
nodes.statement: $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)}=\sum_{i=1}^n[g_i f_t(\mathbf{x}_i)+\tfrac{1}{2}h_i f_t^2(\mathbf{x}_i)]+\Omega(f_t)$ after dropping constants.

nodes.name: Optimal Leaf Weight
nodes.statement: For fixed structure $q$, $w_j^*=-\dfrac{\sum_{i\in I_j} g_i}{\sum_{i\in I_j} h_i+\lambda}$.

nodes.name: Structure Score
nodes.statement: $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)}(q)=-\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^T \dfrac{(\sum_{i\in I_j} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_j} h_i+\lambda}+\gamma T$.

nodes.name: Split Gain
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{L}_{split}=\tfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{(\sum_{i\in I_L} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_L} h_i+\lambda}+\dfrac{(\sum_{i\in I_R} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_R} h_i+\lambda}-\dfrac{(\sum_{i\in I} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I} h_i+\lambda}\right]-\gamma$.

nodes.name: Weighted-Squared-Loss Form of Boosting Objective
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=1}^n \tfrac{1}{2} h_i (f_t(\mathbf{x}_i)-g_i/h_i)^2+\Omega(f_t)+\text{const}$, exhibiting $h_i$ as the per-instance weight in a weighted least-squares regression with target $g_i/h_i$.

nodes.name: Weighted-Quantile Spacing Criterion
nodes.statement: Candidate split points $\{s_{k1},\dots,s_{kl}\}$ satisfy $|r_k(s_{k,j})-r_k(s_{k,j+1})|<\epsilon$ with $s_{k1}=\min_i x_{ik}$, $s_{kl}=\max_i x_{ik}$, giving roughly $1/\epsilon$ candidates.

nodes.name: Tree Boosting Optimization Problem
nodes.statement: Find $\phi=\sum_{k=1}^K f_k$ with $f_k\in\mathcal{F}$ minimizing the regularized objective $\mathcal{L}(\phi)=\sum_i l(\hat{y}_i,y_i)+\sum_k \Omega(f_k)$.

nodes.name: Best-Split Finding
nodes.statement: Given a leaf instance set $I$ and feature dimension $d$, find the feature $k$ and split value that maximizes the split gain $\mathcal{L}_{split}$ in Eq.~(EP271.4).

nodes.name: Weighted Quantile Sketching
nodes.statement: Given a weighted multiset $\mathcal{D}=\{(x_i,w_i)\}$, maintain a small data structure that answers $\epsilon$-approximate weighted-rank queries $r_\mathcal{D}^\pm(y)$ under streaming/distributed insertion, supporting merge and prune.

nodes.name: Exact Greedy Algorithm for Split Finding
nodes.statement: Enumerate all candidate splits on every feature by scanning sorted feature values, accumulating gradient statistics, and tracking the maximum split gain.
output: Split (feature $k$ and threshold) with maximum gain

nodes.name: Approximate Algorithm for Split Finding
nodes.statement: Propose candidate split points by feature percentiles (global or local), bucket instances, aggregate per-bucket gradient statistics, and pick the best split among proposals.

nodes.name: Sparsity-aware Split Finding
nodes.statement: Visit only non-missing entries $I_k$ and learn an optimal default direction at each split by enumerating both `missing-goes-right' and `missing-goes-left' orderings.
output: Split and per-branch default directions with maximum gain

nodes.name: Quantile-Summary Query Function $g(Q,d)$
nodes.statement: Given an $\epsilon$-approximate summary $Q$ and target rank $d$, return the summary point $x^*\in S$ whose midpoint rank brackets $d$.

nodes.name: Weighted Quantile Sketch (Merge + Prune)
nodes.statement: Construct an initial summary, then maintain $\epsilon$-approximation under merge (combine two summaries) and prune (resample to a $b$-element budget via $g(Q,\cdot)$), preserving the same guarantees as the GK summary on weighted data.

nodes.name: Merge Preserves Approximation
nodes.statement: If $Q(\mathcal{D}_1)$ is $\epsilon_1$-approximate and $Q(\mathcal{D}_2)$ is $\epsilon_2$-approximate, then the merged summary $Q(\mathcal{D}_1\cup\mathcal{D}_2)$ is $\max(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$-approximate.
assumptions: Merge is performed as in Appendix A.3

nodes.name: Prune Preserves Approximation
nodes.statement: If $Q'(\mathcal{D})$ is pruned from an $\epsilon$-approximate summary $Q(\mathcal{D})$ with memory budget $b$, then $Q'(\mathcal{D})$ is $(\epsilon+\tfrac{1}{b})$-approximate.

nodes.name: Extended Constraint
nodes.statement: The extended functions $\tilde{r}^-,\tilde{r}^+,\tilde{\omega}$ satisfy $\tilde{r}^-(y)\leq r_\mathcal{D}^-(y)$, $\tilde{r}^+(y)\geq r_\mathcal{D}^+(y)$, $\tilde{\omega}(y)\leq \omega_\mathcal{D}(y)$, and $\tilde{r}^-(y)+\tilde{\omega}(y)\leq \tilde{r}^-(x)$, $\tilde{r}^+(y)\leq \tilde{r}^+(x)-\tilde{\omega}(x)$ for all $y<x$.
assumptions: Domain extension as in Definition DP271.7

nodes.name: Equivalent Pointwise Approximation Conditions
nodes.statement: $Q(\mathcal{D})$ is $\epsilon$-approximate iff $\tilde{r}^+(x_i)-\tilde{r}^-(x_i)-\tilde{\omega}(x_i)\leq \epsilon\omega(\mathcal{D})$ and $\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{r}^-(x_i)-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_i)\leq \epsilon\omega(\mathcal{D})$ for all $i$.

nodes.name: Merge Preserves Extended Identities
nodes.statement: The merged summary satisfies $\tilde{r}^-(y)=\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_1}^-(y)+\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_2}^-(y)$, $\tilde{r}^+(y)=\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_1}^+(y)+\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_2}^+(y)$, and $\tilde{\omega}(y)=\tilde{\omega}_{\mathcal{D}_1}(y)+\tilde{\omega}_{\mathcal{D}_2}(y)$ for all $y\in\mathcal{X}$.
assumptions: Merged summary defined via the rules in Section A.3
conclusions: Pointwise additivity of extended functions over the merge

nodes.name: Query-Function Bracket
nodes.statement: For $\epsilon$-approximate $Q$ and $x^*=g(Q,d)$: $d\geq \tilde{r}^+(x^*)-\tilde{\omega}(x^*)-\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\omega(\mathcal{D})$ and $d\leq \tilde{r}^-(x^*)+\tilde{\omega}(x^*)+\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\omega(\mathcal{D})$.
conclusions: Two-sided rank bracket for the queried point $x^*$

nodes.name: Block-Structure Time Complexity
nodes.statement: On the column-block structure, exact greedy boosting costs $O(Kd\|\mathbf{x}\|_0+\|\mathbf{x}\|_0\log n)$ vs. $O(Kd\|\mathbf{x}\|_0\log n)$ without it; the approximate variant becomes $O(Kd\|\mathbf{x}\|_0+\|\mathbf{x}\|_0\log B)$ vs. $O(Kd\|\mathbf{x}\|_0\log q)$.
assumptions: Block holds at most $B$ rows; $q$ proposal candidates
conclusions: Block structure removes a $\log n$ (resp. $\log q$) factor from per-iteration cost

nodes.name: Proof of Extended Constraint Lemma
nodes.statement: Verify the bounds case-by-case using the construction of the extension on $(x_i,x_{i+1})$ and transitivity of $<$.

nodes.name: Proof of Equivalent Pointwise Approximation Conditions
nodes.statement: For $y\in(x_i,x_{i+1})$ rewrite $\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{r}^-(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)=[\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})]-[\tilde{r}^+(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)]-0$, so the two pointwise constraints imply the global one.

nodes.name: Proof of Merge Theorem
nodes.statement: Bound $\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{r}^-(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)$ on the merge using Lemma LP271.3 and the $\epsilon_i$-approximation of each summand.

nodes.name: Proof of Query-Function Bracket
nodes.statement: Discuss the four cases of $g(Q,d)$ ($x_1$, $x_k$, general $x_i$, general $x_{i+1}$) and bound $d$ using the spacing/extended constraints of $Q$.

nodes.name: Proof of Prune Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP271.4 to consecutive selected points $x'_i,x'_{i+1}$ to bound their gap by $(\epsilon+\tfrac{1}{b})\omega(\mathcal{D})$, fulfilling the iff condition of Lemma LP271.2.

nodes.name: Reduce general $y$ to interval case
nodes.statement: Note the bounds are immediate when $y\leq x_1$ or $y\geq x_k$; the only non-trivial case is $y\in(x_i,x_{i+1})$.

nodes.name: Bound $\tilde{r}^-(y)$ from above
nodes.statement: $\tilde{r}^-(y)=\tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)\leq r_\mathcal{D}^-(x_i)+\omega_\mathcal{D}(x_i)\leq r_\mathcal{D}^-(y)$.

nodes.name: Bound $\tilde{r}^+(y)$ from below
nodes.statement: $\tilde{r}^+(y)=\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})\geq r_\mathcal{D}^+(x_{i+1})-\omega_\mathcal{D}(x_{i+1})\geq r_\mathcal{D}^+(y)$.

nodes.name: Verify spacing inequalities and conclude
nodes.statement: Combine $\tilde{r}^+(x_i)\leq \tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})=\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)$ with the dual lower bound and use transitivity of $<$ to obtain Eq.~(extend-2).

nodes.name: Reduce to interval case
nodes.statement: Boundary cases hold trivially; consider $y\in(x_i,x_{i+1})$.

nodes.name: Telescoping rewrite
nodes.statement: $\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{r}^-(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)=[\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})]-[\tilde{r}^+(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)]-0$.

nodes.name: Combine pointwise constraints
nodes.statement: Adding constraints (constraint22) and (constraint2) at index $i$ bounds the rewrite by $\epsilon\omega(\mathcal{D})$, giving Eq.~(epsdef).

nodes.name: Expand merged $\tilde{r}^+,\tilde{r}^-,\tilde{\omega}$
nodes.statement: Use Lemma LP271.3 to write $\tilde{r}^+(y)-\tilde{r}^-(y)-\tilde{\omega}(y)$ as a sum over $\mathcal{D}_1$ and $\mathcal{D}_2$.

nodes.name: Apply per-summary $\epsilon_i$-approximation
nodes.statement: Each summand is bounded by $\epsilon_i\omega(\mathcal{D}_i)$, so the total is $\leq \epsilon_1\omega(\mathcal{D}_1)+\epsilon_2\omega(\mathcal{D}_2)$.

nodes.name: Bound by max
nodes.statement: $\epsilon_1\omega(\mathcal{D}_1)+\epsilon_2\omega(\mathcal{D}_2)\leq \max(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)\,\omega(\mathcal{D}_1\cup\mathcal{D}_2)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Case $d<\tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_1)+\tilde{r}^+(x_1)]$, $x^*=x_1$
nodes.statement: Use exactness at $x_1$ ($\tilde{r}^-(x_1)=0$, $\tilde{r}^+(x_1)=\tilde{\omega}(x_1)$) to verify both inequalities.

nodes.name: Case $d\geq \tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_k)+\tilde{r}^+(x_k)]$, $x^*=x_k$
nodes.statement: Use $\tilde{r}^+(x_k)=\omega(\mathcal{D})$ and width $\tfrac{1}{2}\tilde{\omega}(x_k)$ to bracket $d$.

nodes.name: General case $x^*=x_i$
nodes.statement: From $2d<\tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)+\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})$ and the $\epsilon$-approximation, derive both rank bounds for $x_i$.

nodes.name: General case $x^*=x_{i+1}$
nodes.statement: Symmetric argument starting from $2d\geq \tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)+\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma LP271.4 at $x'_i$ and $x'_{i+1}$
nodes.statement: Using $x'_i=g(Q,\tfrac{i-1}{b}\omega(\mathcal{D}))$ obtain $\tfrac{i-1}{b}\omega(\mathcal{D})\pm\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\omega(\mathcal{D})$ brackets on $\tilde{r}^\pm(x'_i)\pm\tilde{\omega}(x'_i)$.

nodes.name: Combine consecutive brackets
nodes.statement: Subtracting the two bracket inequalities yields $\tilde{r}^+(x'_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x'_{i+1})-\tilde{r}^-(x'_i)-\tilde{\omega}(x'_i)\leq (\tfrac{1}{b}+\epsilon)\omega(\mathcal{D})$.

nodes.name: Conclude $(\epsilon+1/b)$-approximation via Lemma LP271.2
nodes.statement: The combined inequality is exactly Eq.~(constraint2) for $Q'$ with parameter $\epsilon+1/b$, and (constraint22) is inherited from $Q$.

nodes.name: Initialize gain and global stats
nodes.statement: $gain\leftarrow 0$; $G\leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} g_i$, $H\leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} h_i$.

nodes.name: Loop over features $k=1\ldots m$
nodes.statement: For each feature $k$ reset $G_L\leftarrow 0,H_L\leftarrow 0$ and scan instances in order of $\mathbf{x}_{jk}$.

nodes.name: Update accumulators and best score
nodes.statement: $G_L\leftarrow G_L+g_j$, $H_L\leftarrow H_L+h_j$; set $G_R=G-G_L$, $H_R=H-H_L$ and $score\leftarrow \max(score,\frac{G_L^2}{H_L+\lambda}+\frac{G_R^2}{H_R+\lambda}-\frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$.

nodes.name: Return best split
nodes.statement: Output the split with maximum accumulated score.

nodes.name: Propose candidate splits per feature
nodes.statement: For $k=1\ldots m$, propose $S_k=\{s_{k1},\dots,s_{kl}\}$ by feature percentiles, either globally (per tree) or locally (per split).

nodes.name: Bucket-aggregate gradient statistics
nodes.statement: For each $(k,v)$ accumulate $G_{kv}=\sum_{j: s_{k,v}\geq x_{jk}>s_{k,v-1}} g_j$ and $H_{kv}=\sum_{j} h_j$ in the corresponding bucket.

nodes.name: Find best split among proposals
nodes.statement: Apply the same scoring as the exact algorithm but only over the proposed bucket boundaries.

nodes.name: Initialize gain and global stats over $I$
nodes.statement: $gain\leftarrow 0$; $G\leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} g_i$, $H\leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} h_i$.

nodes.name: Branch: enumerate with missing values going right
nodes.statement: For each feature $k$, scan $I_k$ in ascending order of $\mathbf{x}_{jk}$, accumulating $G_L,H_L$ and updating $score$; this corresponds to assigning missing instances to the right child.

nodes.name: Branch: enumerate with missing values going left
nodes.statement: For each feature $k$, scan $I_k$ in descending order accumulating $G_R,H_R$ and updating $score$; this corresponds to assigning missing instances to the left child.

nodes.name: Return split and default direction
nodes.statement: Output the split (feature, threshold) and per-branch default direction maximizing gain across both enumerations.

nodes.name: Boundary returns
nodes.statement: If $d<\tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_1)+\tilde{r}^+(x_1)]$ return $x_1$; if $d\geq \tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_k)+\tilde{r}^+(x_k)]$ return $x_k$.

nodes.name: Locate bracket index $i$
nodes.statement: Find $i$ with $\tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{r}^+(x_i)]\leq d<\tfrac{1}{2}[\tilde{r}^-(x_{i+1})+\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})]$.

nodes.name: Choose $x_i$ vs $x_{i+1}$ via midpoint test
nodes.statement: If $2d<\tilde{r}^-(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}(x_i)+\tilde{r}^+(x_{i+1})-\tilde{\omega}(x_{i+1})$ return $x_i$, else return $x_{i+1}$.

nodes.name: Construct initial $0$-approximate summary
nodes.statement: From small input multiset $\mathcal{D}$, set $S=\{x:(x,w)\in\mathcal{D}\}$ and $\tilde{r}^\pm(x)=r_\mathcal{D}^\pm(x)$, $\tilde{\omega}(x)=\omega_\mathcal{D}(x)$ for $x\in S$.

nodes.name: Merge two summaries
nodes.statement: Take union of supports and add extended functions pointwise: $\tilde{r}^\pm(x_i)=\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_1}^\pm(x_i)+\tilde{r}_{\mathcal{D}_2}^\pm(x_i)$, $\tilde{\omega}(x_i)=\tilde{\omega}_{\mathcal{D}_1}(x_i)+\tilde{\omega}_{\mathcal{D}_2}(x_i)$.

nodes.name: Prune to memory budget $b$
nodes.statement: Set $S'=\{x'_1,\dots,x'_{b+1}\}$ with $x'_i=g(Q,\tfrac{i-1}{b}\omega(\mathcal{D}))$, restrict $\tilde{r}^\pm,\tilde{\omega}$ to $S'$, and remove duplicates.

nodes.name: Higgs Boson Classification (Exact Greedy Comparison)
nodes.statement: On Higgs-1M dataset (28 features, 1M instances), XGBoost (0.6841 sec/tree, AUC 0.8304) is compared to scikit-learn (28.51 sec/tree, AUC 0.8302) and R.gbm (1.032 sec/tree, AUC 0.6224); XGBoost is >10x faster than scikit-learn at matching accuracy.

nodes.name: Yahoo! LTRC Learning-to-Rank
nodes.statement: On Yahoo! LTRC (473K queries, 700 features) XGBoost achieves NDCG@10 0.7892 at 0.826 sec/tree vs. pGBRT 0.7915 at 2.576 sec/tree; column subsampling improves runtime and ranking quality (NDCG 0.7913).

nodes.name: Allstate-10K Sparsity-Aware Speedup
nodes.statement: On Allstate-10K (sparsity from one-hot encoding) the sparsity-aware algorithm AP271.3 runs >50x faster than a naive dense implementation.

nodes.name: Criteo Out-of-core Experiment
nodes.statement: On the Criteo 1.7B-row click log on a single AWS c3.8xlarge, block compression yields ~3x speedup, two-disk sharding adds another ~2x, enabling end-to-end processing of 1.7B examples on a single machine.

nodes.name: Distributed Criteo on EC2 (vs Spark MLlib, H2O)
nodes.statement: On 32 m3.2xlarge EC2 nodes, XGBoost runs 10x faster per iteration than Spark MLlib and 2.2x faster than H2O, scaling smoothly to 1.7B examples by exploiting out-of-core computation.

nodes.name: Shrinkage and Column Subsampling
nodes.statement: Shrinkage scales newly added weights by factor $\eta$ to leave room for future trees; column (feature) subsampling, borrowed from Random Forests, prevents over-fitting and speeds up the parallel algorithm.

nodes.name: Cache-aware Prefetching
nodes.statement: An internal per-thread buffer fetches gradient statistics in mini-batches, converting an immediate read/write dependency into a longer one and roughly doubling exact-greedy throughput on large datasets.

nodes.name: Block Size Trade-off
nodes.statement: Block size balances parallelization (too small wastes threads) against cache misses (too large overflows L2/L3); $2^{16}$ rows per block is empirically optimal.

nodes.name: Block Compression and Sharding
nodes.statement: Per-column compression (16-bit row offsets, ~26-29% ratio) and round-robin sharding across disks reduce the disk-IO bottleneck of out-of-core training.

nodes.name: GK Quantile Summary (cited)
nodes.statement: There exists a quantile summary supporting merge with $\epsilon\to\max(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ and prune with $\epsilon\to \epsilon+\tfrac{1}{b}$, achieving relative-rank accuracy $\epsilon$ for unweighted streaming data.
assumptions: Unweighted streaming input of comparable items
conclusions: Prune to $b+1$ elements increases approximation error by $1/b$
nodes.origin_citation: Greenwald & Khanna SIGMOD 2001; Zhang & Wang SSDBM

nodes.name: Gradient Tree Boosting (cited)
nodes.statement: Friedman's additive functional-gradient procedure that fits a regression tree to the negative gradient of the loss at each round; XGBoost extends this with a second-order term and explicit regularization.
nodes.origin_citation: Friedman 2001 (greedy function approximation); Friedman et al. 2000 (additive logistic regression)
